nodes.name: 📥 Lead Intake Webhook
nodes.notes:
ENTRY POINT — Receives new leads from website contact forms, landing pages, or any external source.

Expected JSON payload:
{
  'name': 'John Smith',
  'email': 'john@company.com',
  'company': 'Acme Corp',
  'message': 'We need help with our automation...'
}

Webhook URL: https://your-n8n.com/webhook/lead-intake

Integrate with:
- Webflow forms
- Typeform (via Zapier webhook)
- WordPress Contact Form 7
- Any custom HTML form

Alternative trigger: Use 'Google Sheets Trigger' node to watch for new rows.

nodes.name: 🧹 Validate & Clean Lead Data
nodes.notes:
Cleans and validates all incoming lead fields.

Validation rules:
- name: min 2 chars
- email: valid format regex
- company: required
- message: min 10 chars

Enrichment:
- Extracts firstName for personalisation
- Detects free email domains (B2B filter)
- Generates unique leadId
- Sets initial status = 'New'

Throws error on invalid data → caught by Error Trigger workflow.

nodes.name: 🔍 Google Sheets: Duplicate Check
nodes.notes:
Checks if email already exists in the Leads sheet.

Looks up the 'Email' column in the 'Leads' tab.

Returns:
- Empty array → NEW lead (proceed)
- Row data → DUPLICATE (skip)

This prevents sending duplicate emails to the same person.

nodes.name: 🔀 IF: New Lead (Not Duplicate)?
nodes.notes:
Routes based on duplicate check result.

TRUE  → Email not found in sheet → NEW LEAD → continue pipeline
FALSE → Email already in sheet  → DUPLICATE → send 200 OK to webhook and stop

This is the deduplication gate.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: true, message: 'Lead already exists in our system.', email: $json.email }) }}

nodes.name: ⛔ Duplicate: Acknowledge & Stop
nodes.notes:
Returns 200 OK to the form/webhook source for duplicate leads.
Does NOT add to CRM or send any email.
Graceful handling — no error shown to user.

values.content:
You are an expert B2B sales copywriter. Your job is to: 1. Score the lead (1-10) based on quality signals 2. Generate a warm, personalised outreach email 3. Suggest relevant tags You MUST respond with ONLY valid JSON — no markdown, no preamble: { "score": , "scoreLabel": "hot" | "warm" | "cold", "scoreReason": "<1 sentence>", "tags": ["", ""], "emailSubject": "", "emailBody": "", "calendarCTA": "" } SCORING GUIDE: - hot (8-10): Business email, specific technical need, mentions budget/urgency/team - warm (5-7): Business email, general need, vague requirement - cold (1-4): Free email, very short message, no clear business need EMAIL RULES: - Address them by first name - Reference their company name - Mention their specific problem/message - Tone: professional, warm, and helpful — NOT pushy - Include a clear CTA to book a call - Keep under 200 words - Use basic HTML:

, , tags only TAGGING RULES: Choose 2-4 relevant tags from: [automation, saas, agency, startup, enterprise, ecommerce, marketing, development, consulting, finance, healthcare, education, high-priority, follow-up-needed]

nodes.name: 🤖 OpenAI: Score + Personalise Email
nodes.notes:
CORE AI NODE — Does 3 things in one call:

1. LEAD SCORING (1-10):
   hot  (8-10): High-intent, business email, specific need
   warm (5-7):  Moderate intent, some signals
   cold (1-4):  Low signal, free email, vague message

2. EMAIL PERSONALISATION:
   - References their exact message
   - Mentions company name
   - Addresses specific pain point
   - Professional but warm tone
   - Clear booking CTA

3. TAGGING:
   - Automatically categorises lead by industry/need

Model: gpt-4o-mini (cheap, fast, excellent quality)
Temp: 0.7 (creative but focused)
Output: Strict JSON (no markdown wrappers)

nodes.name: 🔧 Parse AI Response + Add Calendar
nodes.notes:
Safely parses AI JSON response.

Fallback handling:
- JSON.parse fails → uses default template
- Score out of range → clamped to 1-10
- Missing scoreLabel → derived from score

Calendar injection:
Appends a styled CTA button linking to CALENDAR_BOOKING_URL env var.

Outputs complete lead object ready for:
- Google Sheets storage
- Email sending
- Slack notification

nodes.name: 📊 Google Sheets: Add Lead Row
nodes.notes:
Adds new lead to 'Leads' tab in Google Sheets CRM.

Columns written:
Lead ID | Name | Email | Company | Message |
Score | Score Label | Score Reason | Tags | Status |
Follow-up Count | Received At | Email Sent At |
Follow-up 1 At | Follow-up 2 At | Replied At | Notes

Sheet must have these headers in Row 1.
See google_sheets_setup.md for full structure.

nodes.name: 📧 Gmail: Send Initial Outreach
nodes.notes:
Sends the AI-personalised initial outreach email.

Dynamic fields:
- sendTo: lead's email
- subject: AI-generated subject line
- body: AI-generated HTML with calendar CTA button

replyTo: YOUR_EMAIL env var (your business email)
So when lead replies, it goes to your inbox.

Alternative: Replace with SMTP node for other email providers.

nodes.name: 📊 Sheets: Update Status → Contacted
nodes.notes:
Updates the lead row status to 'Contacted' after email is sent.

Match key: Email column
Updates:
- Status: Contacted
- Email Sent At: current timestamp

nodes.name: 📱 Telegram: New Lead Alert
nodes.notes:
Sends Telegram notification for every new lead.

Includes:
- Lead name, company, email
- AI score + label (hot/warm/cold)
- Score reasoning
- Message preview (150 chars)
- Confirmation email was sent

Alternative: Replace with Slack node.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: true, leadId: $json.leadId, score: $json.score, scoreLabel: $json.scoreLabel, message: 'Lead processed successfully. Personalised email sent.' }) }}

nodes.name: ✅ Webhook: Success Response
nodes.notes:
Returns HTTP 200 to the form/source after successful processing.
Includes leadId and score in response.
The website can show a custom success message.

nodes.name: ⏳ Wait: 3 Days (Follow-up 1)
nodes.notes:
Pauses workflow for 3 days before checking if lead has replied.

This runs ASYNCHRONOUSLY — the webhook has already responded.
The workflow resumes after 3 days.

In production: n8n stores the paused state and resumes automatically.

Adjust timing:
- Hot leads: 2 days
- Warm leads: 3 days
- Cold leads: 4-5 days

nodes.name: 🔍 Sheets: Check Reply Status
nodes.notes:
After 3-day wait, re-reads the lead row from Sheets.

Why re-read? Because the status may have changed:
- If lead replied → status = 'Replied' (updated by Gmail trigger)
- If lead converted → status = 'Converted'
- If still 'Contacted' → no reply yet → send follow-up

Returns current row data including Status field.

nodes.name: 🔀 IF: No Reply Yet? (FU1)
nodes.notes:
Checks if lead has replied before sending Follow-up 1.

Status == 'Contacted' → No reply → send follow-up
Status == 'Replied' OR 'Converted' → Has replied → stop workflow

This prevents sending follow-ups to people who already engaged.

values.content:
You are a friendly B2B sales follow-up specialist. Write a brief, non-pushy follow-up email.

Rules:
- Keep it under 100 words
- Acknowledge they may be busy
- Add a new value point or insight not mentioned before
- Different from the initial email — do NOT repeat the same message
- End with a soft CTA
- Return ONLY JSON: { "subject": "...", "body": "<HTML>" }

nodes.name: 🤖 AI: Generate Follow-up 1
nodes.notes:
Generates a different, non-repetitive follow-up email.

Key differences from initial email:
- Shorter (under 100 words)
- Acknowledges they may be busy
- Adds a new value point
- Softer, less salesy tone

Cost: ~$0.0001 per follow-up

nodes.name: 🔧 Parse Follow-up 1 Email
nodes.notes:
Parses Follow-up 1 AI response with fallback.
Injects calendar booking button.
Merges with original lead data from Sheets.

nodes.name: 📧 Gmail: Send Follow-up 1
nodes.notes:
Sends AI-generated Follow-up 1 email.
Same replyTo as initial email for reply tracking.

nodes.name: 📊 Sheets: Log Follow-up 1 Sent
nodes.notes:
Records that Follow-up 1 was sent.
Updates Follow-up Count = 1
Records exact timestamp.

nodes.name: ⏳ Wait: 3 More Days (Follow-up 2)
nodes.notes: Waits another 3 days after Follow-up 1 before checking for reply again.

nodes.name: 🔍 Sheets: Check Reply (Pre FU2)
nodes.notes:
Re-reads lead status before sending Follow-up 2.
If replied between FU1 and FU2, stops the chain.

nodes.name: 🔀 IF: Still No Reply? (FU2)
nodes.notes:
Last chance check before sending final follow-up.
Status == 'Contacted' → still no reply → send FU2
Status == 'Replied' → replied! → stop, workflow ends gracefully

values.content:
Write a final, graceful closing follow-up email. This is the last contact attempt.

Rules:
- Maximum 60 words
- Acknowledge this is the last email
- Leave the door open for future contact
- Zero pressure
- Friendly and professional
- Return ONLY JSON: { "subject": "...", "body": "<HTML>" }

nodes.name: 🤖 AI: Generate Follow-up 2 (Final)
nodes.notes:
Generates the FINAL follow-up email.

Tone is completely different:
- Much shorter (60 words max)
- Graceful closing
- Zero pressure
- 'Leaving the door open' style
- No hard CTA

nodes.name: 🔧 Parse Follow-up 2 Email
nodes.notes: Parses final follow-up email. NO calendar button on last email — too pushy.

nodes.name: 📧 Gmail: Send Follow-up 2 (Final)
nodes.notes: Sends the final, graceful closing follow-up email.

nodes.name: 📊 Sheets: Log Follow-up 2 Complete
nodes.notes:
Final update after 2 follow-ups with no reply.
Status → 'Follow-up Complete'
Sequence is now finished for this lead.

nodes.name: ⚡ Error Trigger
nodes.notes:
Fires when ANY node in this workflow throws an error.

To enable:
1. Go to Workflow Settings
2. Set 'Error Workflow' to this same workflow
3. This Error Trigger will catch all failures

Receives: executionId, errorMessage, failedNode, workflow name

nodes.name: 🔍 Classify Error
nodes.notes:
Classifies the error type:
- VALIDATION_ERROR: bad input data
- OPENAI_QUOTA: API rate limit
- SHEETS_ERROR: Google Sheets API
- EMAIL_SEND_FAILURE: Gmail issue
- NOTIFICATION_FAILURE: Telegram

Each gets severity level and a fix suggestion.

nodes.name: 📊 Sheets: Log Error
nodes.notes:
Logs error to 'ErrorLogs' sheet tab.
Provides permanent audit trail.
continueOnFail: true — if Sheets fails, still send Telegram alert.

nodes.name: 📱 Telegram: Error Alert
nodes.notes:
Sends immediate Telegram alert on any error.
Includes error type, failed node, and fix suggestion.
